business_scope.primary_industry_name: Die-Struck Brass Cloisonné Polishing of Novelty Enamel Badges

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law of French tradition applicable to private law in Quebec; Common Law applicable to federal and other provincial matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) (provisionally applied since 2017)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) (2018)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA) (2014)
Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (1986)
Convention between Canada and France for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1975, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC regulations; Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c S-31.1, arts. 11.1-11.10 (register of individuals with significant control) and Regulation respecting the register of individuals with significant control, CQLR c S-31.1, r 3.1; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 20.1-20.7 (federal equivalent regime); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss. 83.01-83.33 (terrorist financing and listed entities).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of incorporation (statuts de constitution) — certified true copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises Québec (REQ); alternate: Corporations Canada for federal route
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by Authentication Services, Global Affairs Canada (Canada has been a Party to the Hague Apostille Convention since 24 January 2024); Consular Legalization where the destination state is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Attestation de conformité / certificat de statut (certificate of status and standing of the enterprise)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Authentication Services, Global Affairs Canada, or Consular Legalization for non-Hague destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of individuals with significant control (registre des personnes ayant un contrôle significatif) — pre-incorporation draft excerpt certified by corporate counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate counsel licensed by the Barreau du Québec, corroborated by REQ filings subsequent to incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization in accordance with the receiving financial institution's KYC/AML acceptance policy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled/legalized copies of each proposed beneficial owner's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the home state is a Hague member; otherwise Consular Legalization by the Canadian diplomatic or consular mission accredited to the home state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Name search report — attestation de recherche de nom (evidence of name clearance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises Québec (REQ); for federal route, NUANS report from Corporations Canada's designated provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Generally not apostilled for domestic use; if demanded by a foreign bank or regulator, apostilled via Authentication Services, Global Affairs Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all proposed directors, officers, shareholders, and individuals with significant control against: (i) Canada's Consolidated Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, the United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2, and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 13; (ii) the Criminal Code (Canada) List of Terrorist Entities maintained by the RCMP; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists where USD-denominated payments are processed through Stripe or Etsy Direct Pay; and (v) EU sanctions lists for payment rails routed through the European Economic Area. PEP determination follows FINTRAC's PCMLTFA guidance on domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, including the five-year post-office cooling-off monitoring period, enhanced client due diligence for any person identified as PEP or PEP-adjacent, and continuous transaction monitoring throughout the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises Québec (REQ) Online Services portal (services.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/cd-dgc.nsf/eng/home)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (Charte de la langue française), CQLR c C-11, ss. 63(3) and 69(2), the corporation must adopt a French-language name and the corporate legal element must appear in a French form (Incorporée/Inc., Société par actions, Limitée/Ltée). Bilingual names are accepted only where the French version is present and predominant. Non-Latin-script names (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated into a Latin-script French form; numerals and foreign-language descriptive tokens are disfavored unless commonly used with a standard French rendition. The name must satisfy arts. 12-16 QBCA: it must not be identical or similar to an existing reserved or registered name, must not mislead regarding the nature or identity of the enterprise, and must not be obscene, contemptuous, or contrary to public order.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Trust / Fiducie / Insurance / Assurance — requires prior authorization of the Minister of Finance, OSFI, or the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF)
Université / University / Collège / College — requires prior approval of the Minister of Higher Education
Reine / Royale / Royal / Couronne / Crown / Gouvernement / Government / Municipal / Commission / Agent — tokens implying a connection with the Crown or a public authority
Barreau / Law Society / Avocat / Lawyer / Notaire / Notary — reserved for members of regulated professional orders
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Valeurs mobilières / Securities / Fonds / Fund — regulated financial tokens requiring AMF registration
Coopérative / Cooperative / Société mutuelle — statutorily defined designations reserved for specific legal forms
Criminal Code offence descriptors (e.g., Terrorist, Terroriste, Crime, Criminal) and any token scandalous, obscene, defamatory, or contrary to public order
Inc. / Corp. / Ltd. / S.A. / SARL — use limited to the legally adopted corporate element of the relevant incorporation statute
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by REQ, the promoter may: (1) file a revised name and pay the applicable new search fee through the REQ online portal; (2) request a written administrative re-examination where the rejection rests on an arguable error of law or fact; (3) apply for judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec under arts. 529-561 of the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01, within the statutory delay; or (4) incorporate under the assigned matriculation number (constitution sans nom / numéro matricule) and adopt a compliant name by subsequent articles of amendment (statuts de modification). For the federal CBCA route, a written reconsideration request may be submitted to the Director, Corporations Canada, within 30 days, with the NUANS reservation extendable for one further period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole registered office. Under art. 8 QBCA, the head office (siège social) must be situated in Quebec at a determinate physical address where corporate records are kept and service of process may validly be effected; REQ rejects post-office boxes and pure virtual mail-forwarding addresses. A home-based workshop actually used by the enamel-pin business, or a serviced-office suite located in Quebec that is capable of receiving legal process, is permissible; a Quebec corporate registered agent may provide such a physical address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5-10% cumulative probability within the first 24 months, arising principally from Revenu Québec GST/QST and source-deduction compliance verifications and occasional REQ address-integrity checks; unannounced on-site warranty inspection is not anticipated for a low-risk non-licensed merchandise manufacturer, with tax audit visits constituting the main quantified trigger.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and clearance — attestation de recherche de nom (REQ online request)
Filing of articles of incorporation (statuts de constitution) and enterprise registration (déclaration d'immatriculation)
Legal fees — drafting of articles of incorporation, by-laws, directors' consent resolutions, minute book, and register of individuals with significant control
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard QBCA incorporation package (CAD 1,000-1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of director and shareholder identity declarations and consent forms (notarial deed where required by counsel or receiving bank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary of the Chambre des notaires du Québec

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign-issued KYC and UBO documentation (approximately three documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authentication Services, Global Affairs Canada, and applicable consular missions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (CAD 10 per authentication by Global Affairs Canada) plus applicable consular fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: One-time PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic consolidated sanctions screening of proposed directors, shareholders, and UBOs via commercial AML screening platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for one-time onboarding screening of up to five natural persons

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered office physical address arrangement in Quebec (serviced-office or registered-agent address capable of service of process)
Contingency reserve for name rejection appeal, revised search report, or re-filing of articles
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1 (Loi sur les societes par actions, RLRQ c S-31.1), ss. 11-15 (incorporation and articles), s. 18 (powers), s. 54 (registered office), s. 59 (first directors), s. 116 (officers), s. 119 (by-laws); read with the Regulation respecting the application of the Business Corporations Act (Quebec) and the Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — Direction de l'immatriculation et de la constitution; public register maintained under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (Statuts de constitution, Form T-2) executed in French and filed electronically through the REQ 'Constitution d'une personne morale' online portal; issuance of the attestation de constitution and the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow requirement. The corporation may issue no-par-value common shares; the board must determine the adequacy of the consideration received before issuing certificates, and the paid-up capital account is credited accordingly. Non-cash consideration requires board approval and, in cases of potential shareholder prejudice, an independent valuation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION (Enacted by written resolution of the sole incorporator and first director) BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscription for ten thousand (10,000) no-par common shares by the incorporator is accepted, and certificates shall be issued after payment of the authorized consideration. 2. The registered office of the Corporation be established at 4000 De Maisonneuve Boulevard West, Suite 1100, Montreal, Quebec, H3Z 1J9, Canada. 3. The following persons are appointed as officers: [Name] as President and [Name] as Secretary-Treasurer. 4. The proposed by-laws of the Corporation are adopted as approved. 5. The Corporation is authorized to open and operate banking accounts with [Financial Institution], with Signing Authorities as designated. All decisions are unanimously approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — Name Research Service and the national NUANS database (Recherche de nom et réservation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed French-language corporate name (with legal element 'société par actions', 'inc.' or 'corp.') together with two alternative names. The REQ runs a NUANS search against Canadian corporate and trademark records. The resulting name search report is valid for 150 days and constitutes the basis for name reservation at the time of incorporation. The name must not be prohibited, misleading, or confusing and must satisfy the French-language requirements of the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11).
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in French (with permitted English abbreviation)
Two alternate corporate names
NUANS name search request form or electronic dashboard submission
Proof of identity of the incorporator, if physical filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, the applicant may submit a revised name with a new NUANS report, or contest the REQ decision by administrative complaint under s. 15 of the BCA within 30 days; the Registraire accepts corrective refilings without loss of priority if the report is still valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — Constitution en ligne transactional portal (Inscription d'une personne morale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and electronically sign Form T-2 (articles of incorporation) on the REQ portal. Provide the reserved name, the class structure and share rights, the first directors' full names and residential addresses, the Quebec registered office address, and the incorporator statements. Pay the prescribed filing fee by credit card. Upon acceptance, the REQ issues the attestation de constitution and the NEQ identification number; the corporation exists as of the date of the attestation (s. 15 BCA).
required_dossiers: Signed articles of incorporation (Form T-2) drafted in French
Valid NUANS name search report (issued within 150 days)
Consent of each first director (Form N-2 or annex)
Quebec registered office street address
Filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is queried or refused, the REQ issues a notice of incompleteness; the applicant must respond within 30 days with corrected articles and supporting consents. A late or unaddressed refusal requires a new filing and new fee. Post-issuance clerical defects are cured by filing an Avis de correction and obtaining a corrected attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office and Appointment of First Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) and the corporation's internal first organizational meeting process
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered office address is a physical location in Quebec and must appear in the articles or be declared to the REQ. Following the attestation, the incorporators convene the first organizational meeting (or act by written resolution) to adopt by-laws, elect or confirm the first directors, appoint officers (President, Secretary-Treasurer, and any other required officers), and authorize corporate banking. The REQ must be notified of directors and officers through a Déclaration de renseignements mise à jour within 60 days of any change.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first organizational meeting or signed written resolution
Corporate by-laws (reglements internes) adopted by the board
Declaration of registered office (Form A-1), if not included in articles
Consents to act and specimen signatures of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to file required updates with the REQ within 60 days may attract an administrative penalty; the obligation is cured by filing a corrective Déclaration de mise à jour online and paying the applicable late-filing fee. Defective officer appointments are ratified by subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Subscription and Issuance of Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal corporate records; no external approval required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board accepts the share subscription, fixes the consideration in Canadian dollars, authorizes issuance of the subscribed common shares, and instructs issuance of duly signed certificates. The certificates must comply with the by-laws and, where applicable, bear the corporate seal and the signatures of the authorized officers. The share capital account and paid-up capital are recorded; the register of share transfers is updated.
required_dossiers: Executed share subscription agreement
First board resolution approving the issuance and consideration
Share certificate stub and cancelled certificate specimen
Bank deposit slip or proof of consideration received
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If shares are issued for non-cash consideration, a valuation by a certified public accountant should be obtained to avoid a shareholder oppression claim; any defective issuance is remedied by a new board resolution, cancellation of the irregular certificate, and reissue against a proper certificate stub.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations — NEQ, GST/QST, and Payroll Accounts (Revenu Quebec / CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec (administration of GST, QST, provincial corporate tax and source deductions) and the Canada Revenue Agency (federal corporate income tax account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The NEQ is assigned automatically upon incorporation. Register the corporation with Revenu Quebec for the Quebec sales tax (TVQ/QST), the GST/HST, provincial corporate income tax, and payroll source deductions (income tax, Quebec Parental Insurance Plan, Quebec Pension Plan) under the Act respecting the Quebec sales tax and the Taxation Act. Concurrently open a Business Number account with the CRA for federal corporate income tax and GST registration in the federal system. Apply to CNESST for workers' compensation coverage if employees are hired.
required_dossiers: Attestation de constitution and NEQ confirmation
Completed Revenu Quebec registration form (Demande d'inscription, LM-101-V)
Corporate banking details
Payroll information and employer classification for CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Delayed registration may be accepted with a written explanation and retroactive effective date if filed within a reasonable period; where interest or penalties are assessed, the corporation may file a notice of objection under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c A-6.002) within 90 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Minute Book, Statutory Registers, and Corporate Records Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and external counsel (the REQ maintains the public record)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate minute book in French, containing the articles, attestation of constitution, by-laws, board and shareholder minutes or written resolutions, registers of directors, shareholders, share transfers and share certificates, and any unanimous shareholder agreement. Maintain the registers current and ensure that each change of director, officer, registered office or share capital is disclosed to the REQ by an updated declaration within 60 days as required by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Copies of articles of incorporation and all REQ attestations
Adopted by-laws and by-law amendments
Share certificate stubs and transfer register
Current list of directors and officers
Consents of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective records are remedied by a ratification resolution of the board and corrective REQ filings; failure to maintain proper corporate records may constitute an offence under s. 273 of the BCA and is cured by prompt regularization with the Registraire and, if necessary, a late-filed declaration with penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupancy and Industrial Establishment Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent local municipality (city where the registered office and workshop are located) — urbanism/inspection services (e.g., Ville de Montreal, Services de l'urbanisme et des permis)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal occupancy permit (permis d'occupation / permis d'affaires) for light industrial manufacturing of enamel lapel pins. Verify that the zoning by-law permits the manufacture of die-struck metal goods and the use of enameling furnaces. Submit building floor plans, proof of lease or ownership, a fire safety certificate, and confirmation of conformity with the applicable construction and fire codes. The permit is site-specific and must be renewed upon change of premises or expanded production capacity.
required_dossiers: Zoning conformity certificate or urbanism testimony
Proof of lease or ownership of the workshop premises
Building floor plan indicating enameling ovens and stamping equipment
Fire safety service clearance (service de securite incendie)
Municipal application form and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused or queried, the corporation may apply for a minor variance (derogation mineure) from the municipal planning committee or file a contestation before the Tribunal administratif du Quebec (TAQ) within 30 days of the refusal; corrected architectural or fire-safety plans may also be resubmitted without a new tariff.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction generale de l'inspection industrielle et des autorisations environnementales, jointly with the competent municipal inspection service.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Attestation d'assainissement (industrial wastewater discharge authorization) under s. 31.1 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) and, where the enameling process emits atmospheric contaminants, a Certificat d'autorisation under s. 22 EQA for the industrial equipment concerned.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Service des autorisations environnementales et du registre des attestations d'assainissement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Declarable category under the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment of certain projects (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23): a small-format hard enamel lapel pin workshop is a light industrial establishment subject to the industrial establishment wastewater register (attestation d'assainissement) but does not require a full environmental impact assessment study unless installed production capacity reaches the thresholds for major industrial projects (e.g., metal finishing with total plating bath volume of 100 litres or more, or annual output exceeding 10 tonnes of finished enamelled goods).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the municipal sewer must comply with the municipal by-law and the Regulation respecting the discharge of water: pH 6.0-9.5, total suspended solids below 30 mg/L, no free cyanide, copper below 1.0 mg/L, nickel below 1.0 mg/L, zinc below 2.0 mg/L. Air emissions: VOC capture and treatment apparatus is required where oven/furnace VOC emissions exceed 10 tonnes per year, with annual emission declaration; below this threshold a simple declaration to MELCCFP suffices. Hazardous waste: enamel residues, epoxy, polychlorinated materials and polishing sludges must be stored in labelled sealed containers, removed by accredited carriers, and tracked by manifest in accordance with the Regulation respecting hazardous materials (CQLR c Q-2, r. 35); direct discharge of process wastewater or sludges to the sewer or the environment is prohibited.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the competent municipal fire prevention service confirming compliance with the Fire Safety Code for heat-producing enameling furnaces and spray booths; structural load clearance by a licensed engineer certifying the floor capacity for stamping presses and kiln installations; occupational health clearance from CNESST for ventilation, noise levels, compressed-air equipment and workplace chemical exposure, together with an emergency preparedness plan including fire extinguishers, first-aid station, and evacuation signage per the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal Service de securite incendie covering the enameling ovens, electrical installation, and storage of flammable enamels; structural load inspection by a professional engineer for the die-stamping presses and kilns; workplace clearance obtained from CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail) for ventilation, exposure to volatile organic compounds, noise and manual handling, with a first-aid and evacuation protocol in place.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal administration of GST/HST, Income Tax Act, and Business Number registrations via My Business Account (portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency); Revenu Québec (RQ) — provincial administration of Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), provincial corporate income tax, and employer contributions (portal: revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation carrying on business in Canada/Quebec must obtain (1) a federal Business Number (BN) with GST/HST, corporate income tax, and payroll program accounts from the CRA (via Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1, RC4601 for non-residents); and (2) a Quebec establishment number (NEQ) from Registraire des entreprises du Québec and a QST account from Revenu Québec (via Form LM-2-V / online 'Mon dossier d'entreprise'). Non-resident applicants must appoint a Canadian resident representative/agent for service, provide proof of foreign incorporation, and may be registered even below the threshold if deemed to be carrying on business in Canada (s. 143(2)(b) ETA) by soliciting orders through the internet, mail order, or employees/agents in Canada. The Etsy Direct Pay/Stripe storefront constitutes solicitation nexus; the BN/GST number must be displayed on invoices and the 'registrant status' must be declared for B2B customers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — An Inc./Corp. business corporation is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act: federal corporate income tax at 15% general rate (9% for manufacturing/processing for CCPCs, plus federal abatement; small business deduction 12.2%; Quebec provincial rate 11.5%; combined top ~27%; all taxable income computed entity-level, no US check-the-box pass-through).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box pass-through entity classification for corporations; available statutory elections include: (i) GST/HST Quick Method and streamlined accounting elections under ETA; (ii) section 85 rollover election on transfer of qualifying property to the corporation at tax-deferred amounts; (iii) CCPC small business deduction and association/related-death elections under ITA s. 125; (iv) QST simplified method elections for small businesses with Revenu Québec; (v) Group relief elections for financial institutions; and (vi) hybrid mismatch/instrument design cautions under GAAR (s. 245 ITA) and Mandatory Disclosure Rules (DAC6/Reportable Transactions, s. 237.1 ITA).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under the Excise Tax Act; Quebec applies the QST (Taxe de vente du Québec) under the Quebec Taxation Act (Loi sur la taxe de vente du Québec) — a non-harmonized VAT-credit system administered separately by Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 — GST/HST: the 'small supplier' threshold is breached when total worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports, capital property, and financial services) exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or over the four immediately preceding consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 148). QST: identical CAD 30,000 threshold under RQ (LTVQ s. 64, Reg. 54). Non-residents soliciting orders in Canada may acquire GST/HST registration status without the threshold; voluntary registration is available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance / continuous transaction control regime exists in Canada. CRA does not require digital stamping or fiscal API approval of invoices; however, registrants must charge GST/HST on taxable supplies, issue tax invoices/credit notes containing prescribed ETA Reg. 242 information, keep six-year records, and file returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE / RQ electronic filing). Quebec has published an e-invoicing roadmap (PEPPOL/EDIFACT based) for mandatory B2B e-invoicing in coming years, but it is not yet in force. Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe transaction records must be retained in machine-readable form as source documents for CRA/RQ audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of tangible personal property (hard enamel lapel pins) are zero-rated for GST/HST and QST when the supplier exports the goods to a non-resident customer removed from Canada "as soon as reasonably possible" after delivery, provided the supplier obtains and retains evidence of export (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 20; LTVQ s. 130 et seq.). The exporter may claim input tax credits (ITC) for inputs related to export sales; domestic supplies in Quebec remain taxable at 14.975%. Services rendered to non-residents (e.g., management graphics design) may qualify under Part V, s. 7 if performed outside Canada or related to real/immovable property located abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A / Export Declaration, or CBSA ACI/CAED e-manifest record; CBSA's Canada Export Reporting System records are required for postal/courier exports above CAD 2,500)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List showing exporter, consignee, HS code 7117.19/8306.29, description "hard enamel lapel pins", quantity, unit price, and total value
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill issued to a non-resident consignee
Proof of delivery outside Canada (signed delivery confirmation, courier tracking, or foreign customs entry evidence such as CBP entry documentation)

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or payment processor settlement record (Etsy Direct Pay / Stripe payout) evidencing foreign exchange repatriation to a Canadian bank account within the FX deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec jointly audit e-commerce export vendors. Unsubstantiated export zero-rating triggers reassessment of the supply at 5% GST plus 9.975% QST retroactively, denial of ITCs, gross-interest charges, and penalties: the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax understated/refund overstated (ETA s. 280(1)); 50% penalty for false statements made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence (s. 280(1)(c)); GST evasion prosecutions up to CAD 200,000 fine and two years' imprisonment (s. 327-328 ETA); RQ equivalents under LTVQ s. 1. VAT clawback exposure includes all past filings within a six-year assessment window (unlimited for fraud).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange monitoring and compliance reporting enforced by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions; the Canadian dollar operates under a free-floating exchange rate regime; no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distributions, interest payments, or capital repatriation; no prior regulatory approval is required for cross-border fund transfers
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or forced conversion requirements exist; export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency accounts indefinitely; cross-border cash or monetary instrument movements exceeding CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC; no mandatory conversion timeline applies

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium feasibility; offshore digital EMIs cannot directly hold settlement accounts at Canadian clearing institutions unless licensed under the Bank Act; they may operate via agent bank arrangements; practical utility is limited to payment facilitation and secondary disbursement, not core treasury account replacement
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not strictly mandated; FINTRAC-compliant remote identification methods are permissible; however, Canadian banks typically require at least one director or authorized signing officer to complete an in-person or remote video identity verification interview, particularly for non-resident directors; certified documents may require legalization or apostille

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or remote beneficial owner controlling the account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports, proof of residential address, federal or Quebec corporate registry extracts, beneficial ownership declaration, corporate organizational chart, source of wealth and source of funds statements, professional references, and FINTRAC-compliant remote identity verification records

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers to jurisdictions under enhanced monitoring or sanctions watchlists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, transport documents, signed sales contracts, Incoterms, Etsy and Stripe payout reports, Canada Border Services Agency customs declarations, and a complete entity transaction history demonstrating legitimate trade flows

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancies between account activity and declared business scope of hard enamel lapel pin manufacturing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated business plan, product catalogs, manufacturing and procurement agreements, supplier due diligence files, and periodic statistical filings under the Canadian International Trade Database

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 from foreign parent or investor via correspondent banking; CAD clearing through Lynx (RTGS) for high-value payments or ACSS for retail batch payments; purpose code should reference 'S001 - General Payment' or corresponding BOP distinction; verification includes source of funds documentation, FX deal confirmation, OFAC and sanctions screening; non-resident investment may require filing under the Investment Canada Act if applicable; no exchange control approval is required
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 on correspondent clearing rails; commercial letters of credit established through an issuing Canadian bank under UCP600; documentary collections and open account terms supported by supply chain finance; settlement currencies typically CAD or USD; outgoing wires above CAD 10,000 trigger FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards on CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and other major currency pairs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or thinly traded currencies as permitted by Canadian bank counterparties
Cross-currency swaps executed under ISDA documentation with licensed Canadian bank dealers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee is CAD $100 (approx. USD $75); continued delinquency leads to administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under Quebec Business Corporations Act and Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than June 15 for the preceding fiscal year; if fiscal year ends between December 1 and March 31, deadline is June 15; otherwise within six months of fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty starts at CAD $10 per month; persistent delinquency triggers administrative revocation of the enterprise registration and loss of corporate powers in Quebec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Registrable Persons Register (Register of Registrable Individuals) confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; filed declaration transmitted via Registraire des entreprises if changes occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation during the annual declaration filing; updates required within 15 days of any change in registrable persons.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the register is an offence; directors and officers may be subject to fines up to CAD $5,000 for each violation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Canada Business Corporations Act and Quebec Business Corporations Act, an independent audit is mandatory for public corporations, corporations subject to prescribed requirements, and distribution-issuing corporations; private corporations may be exempt if gross annual revenues are less than CAD $500,000 and total assets are less than CAD $250,000, subject to shareholder unanimous agreement to waive.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) for public accountable enterprises; Canadian GAAP (ASPE – Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations; the entity may elect ASPE due to private closely-held structure.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec requires a register of registrable persons (UBOs) with at least 25% ownership or control. The register must be accurate as of the annual declaration date; any shareholding transfer or change in control triggers an update within 15 days. The Quebec annual declaration must confirm current directors, registered office, and registrable persons information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Registrable Persons (UBO Register) under Quebec Business Corporations Act

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD $2,500 – $8,000 depending on transaction volume and complexity (low-risk private corporation; waived audit possible if unanimous shareholder consent and revenue/asset exemptions met)

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); 14.0% combined for Canadian-controlled private corporation active business income eligible for the small business deduction on the first C$500,000
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction (federal 9% rate and Quebec 5% rate on the first C$500,000 of qualifying active business income); Quebec reduced rate of 8.5% for qualified manufacturing and processing profits (ISIC 3240 qualifies); federal manufacturing and processing profits deduction incorporated into the 15% general rate; investment tax credits and scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) refundable credits; capital cost allowance accelerated deductions
